claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

test_case.agent_script:
=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 6 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 6 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child in care for 7 weeks (within 8-week limit)
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

expected_eligibility.name: Alex

circumstances: Child in care for 7 weeks (within 8-week limit)

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start by beginning the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about your child or children.

**How old is the child (or children) you're claiming for?**

To help determine your eligibility, I need to know:
- What is the child's current age?
- If you have multiple children, please tell me all of their ages

This is important because Child Benefit has different rules depending on whether children are:
- **Under 16** - generally automatic qualification
- **16-19 years old** - may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- **20 or over** - not eligible for Child Benefit

Please provide the age(s) of the child/children you're asking about.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm interested in finding out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex, who is 6 years old. Does that help?

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. Yes, that helps a lot!

So you have **one child, Alex, who is 6 years old**. Since Alex is under 16, let me move forward with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! Since Alex is 6 years old, the next check is about work. Let me ask:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work)?**

For a 6-year-old child, the answer will almost certainly be "yes" since children this young are typically not in paid employment. But I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, no - Alex doesn't work at all! He's only 6, so he's still in primary school. He just does his schoolwork and plays with his friends.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! That's exactly what I expected for a 6-year-old. So Alex is not in any paid work, which means he meets this requirement.

Let me continue with the next check in the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now let me ask the next question:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right?**

Specifically, I'm asking whether Alex is receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit

in his own name. For a 6-year-old, this is very unlikely, but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just 6, so he doesn't get anything like that himself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex doesn't receive any of those benefits in his own name, which is what we'd expect for a 6-year-old. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now the next question is about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex NOT in a disqualifying apprenticeship?**

For a 6-year-old in primary school, the answer is straightforward - he's not in any apprenticeship at all. However, let me confirm: Is Alex in any kind of apprenticeship programme?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, definitely not! Alex is only 6 - he's just in primary school. He's not in any kind of apprenticeship or training programme.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's exactly what I expected. Alex is 6 years old and in primary school, so he's not in any apprenticeship programme. Let me move forward with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now we need to check your residency status. This is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Can you tell me about your residency situation?** Specifically:

1. **Do you normally live in the UK?**

Or if you're not normally resident in the UK, do any of the following apply to you:
- You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme and are working (earning above the National Insurance threshold)
- You have pre-settled status and are actively seeking work
- You have pre-settled status with sufficient resources to support yourself and family
- You have pre-settled status and are studying with sufficient resources
- You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA or Swiss national
- You're a Crown servant living abroad

Which of these best describes your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK. I live here in England with Alex - we've been here all along.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! That's great. So you normally live in the UK in England with Alex. This means you meet the residency requirements for Child Benefit.

Let me continue with the next check in the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check if you're responsible for Alex. This is the next key requirement.

**Are you responsible for Alex?** This means either:

1. **You live with Alex** - You live in the same household, or
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** - You pay for things like his food, clothes, housing, pocket money, or other essentials, or
3. **You're paying maintenance** - You're making court-ordered or agreed maintenance payments for Alex's care

Which of these applies to your situation? It sounds like you live with Alex since you mentioned you live in England with him - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me. We live together in the same household.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! So you live with Alex in the same household - that clearly shows you're responsible for him. This meets the requirement perfectly.

Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check an important question about other claimants:

**Is anyone else (such as Alex's other parent, a grandparent, or another guardian) currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or could they potentially claim?**

This is important because:
- If no one else is claiming, you can proceed with your claim
- If someone else is claiming but you've both agreed who should claim, that's fine
- If there's a dispute between multiple people about who should claim, HMRC will need to make the decision

So, is there anyone else involved in Alex's care who might also claim for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, there's no one else claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me - I'm his parent and he lives with me, so nobody else is getting it for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! So you're the only one claiming Child Benefit for Alex - there's no other claimant involved. That's clear.

Let me move forward with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check where Alex is living and if any special circumstances apply:

**Where is Alex currently living?** Specifically:

- Is Alex in hospital?
- Is Alex in care (such as local authority care)?
- Is Alex fostered (living with foster carers)?
- Or is Alex living normally at home with you?

Given what you've told me, I expect Alex is living normally at home with you - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, Alex has been in local authority care for a couple of months now. It's been a difficult time for us.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to hear that's been a difficult situation for you. Thank you for being honest about that - it's important information for the assessment.

So Alex is currently in local authority care. Let me navigate to the next check to see how this affects the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Now I need to understand the specifics of Alex's care arrangement:

**Can you tell me:**

1. **How long has Alex been in local authority care?** You mentioned a couple of months - is that approximately 8 weeks or more/less than 8 weeks?

2. **Does Alex spend at least 24 hours a week at home with you?** For example, does he visit you for weekends, or specific days during the week?

This is important because Child Benefit can continue for up to 8 weeks while a child is in care, and there are also exceptions if the child spends significant time at home. These details will determine your eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been about 7 weeks now that he's been in care. And no, he doesn't come home to stay with me - he's at the care home full-time. I visit him there when I can, but he doesn't spend nights at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. So Alex has been in care for about 7 weeks and doesn't spend 24 hours or more per week at home with you. Let me check the details here.

You mentioned Alex has been in care for about 7 weeks. This is important because:
- Child Benefit can continue for up to 8 weeks while a child is in care
- After 8 weeks, eligibility typically ends (unless the child spends at least 24 hours a week at home, which doesn't apply in Alex's case)

Since Alex has been in care for approximately 7 weeks, he's still within the 8-week window where Child Benefit can continue. This means you should still meet this eligibility requirement.

Let me continue with the next check in the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to ask one final important question about payments:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance while he's in care?**

In other words, are you responsible for any payments towards Alex's care, or is the local council covering all of his accommodation and maintenance costs?

This is a key requirement - generally, you cannot claim Child Benefit if the local council is fully paying for the child's care.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying me anything. I'm not receiving any maintenance or payments from the local authority for Alex while he's in care.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Just to make sure I have this right - you're saying that **the local council IS paying for Alex's accommodation and maintenance** (they're covering his care costs), but **you are NOT receiving any direct payments from them**.

Let me confirm the situation:
- The local council is paying the care home/facility to look after Alex
- You are not receiving any financial payments or support from the council

Is that correct? This distinction is important because the rule is about whether the council is paying **for the child's care**, not whether you personally receive money.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see what you mean. Yes, that's right - the local council is paying for Alex's care at the care home. They're covering all his accommodation and maintenance costs there. I'm not the one paying for it.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I understand the situation now. Since the local council is paying for Alex's accommodation and maintenance at the care home, this affects your Child Benefit eligibility.

Let me navigate to see what this means for your claim.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm afraid I have some disappointing news regarding your Child Benefit eligibility for Alex.

## Assessment Result: **INELIGIBLE**

**Reason:** You cannot claim Child Benefit for Alex because the local council is paying towards his accommodation and maintenance while he's in care.

### Explanation:

While Alex met several of the eligibility criteria:
- ✅ He is under 16 years old
- ✅ He is not working full-time
- ✅ You normally live in the UK
- ✅ You are responsible for him as his parent
- ✅ He has been in care for less than 8 weeks (still within the grace period)

However, the key disqualifying factor is that **the local council is covering all of Alex's accommodation and maintenance costs** while he's in local authority care. The Child Benefit rules state that you cannot receive Child Benefit if the local council is paying for the child's accommodation or maintenance.

### What This Means:

This is a standard rule for children in local authority care where the council is meeting their costs. Once this arrangement changes (for example, if Alex returns home to you), you may become eligible to claim Child Benefit again.

### Next Steps:

- If Alex's circumstances change and he returns to living with you, you would likely become eligible for Child Benefit again
- You can contact HMRC or check the Gov.uk website (https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility) for more information
- If you have any concerns about this decision, you can appeal or seek further advice from the Citizens Advice Bureau or a similar organisation

I'm sorry this isn't the outcome you were hoping for. Is there anything else I can help clarify about this decision?

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I understand this is likely a difficult situation given the circumstances you're facing. If you have any questions about this decision or if Alex's situation changes in the future, please don't hesitate to contact HMRC or seek advice from a support organisation.

reasonings: Alex is 6 years old (under 16, meeting age requirement). He is not in paid work (meets work requirement). He does not receive benefits in his own name (meets benefit requirement). He is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship (meets apprenticeship requirement). The claimant is normally resident in the UK in England (meets residency requirement). The claimant lives with Alex and is responsible for him (meets responsibility requirement). There is no other claimant for Alex (meets claimant requirement). Alex has been in local authority care for approximately 7 weeks, which is within the 8-week grace period for children in care. However, the local council is paying for Alex's full accommodation and maintenance at the care home. The rules state that Child Benefit cannot be claimed if the local council is paying towards the child's accommodation or maintenance. This is a disqualifying factor that makes the claimant INELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.
arguments.overall_reasoning: The claimant would ordinarily be eligible for Child Benefit for their 6-year-old son Alex, as Alex meets all the standard eligibility criteria (under 16, not working, not in disqualifying apprenticeship). The claimant is also eligible in terms of residency (normally resident in UK) and responsibility (living with and caring for Alex). However, because Alex is currently in local authority care with the local council paying for his full accommodation and maintenance costs, the claimant is disqualified from claiming Child Benefit. This is a standard rule for children in local authority care where the council meets their living costs."
